# UI Chesed — Clean Futuristic Observatory

The Awtsmoos renews the visible vessel before the eye can call it interface;
Awtsmoos.com should reveal enormous capability through calm hierarchy, air, and grace.

## Product intent

The Observatory is an expert instrument, not the human social network itself. The UI must make that distinction obvious while remaining inviting: one primary path into Social Hub, one compact expert workspace, advanced context only when requested, safe reads visually dominant, mutations visibly guarded, exact evidence retractable.

## Visual obligations

- Scope every Observatory selector beneath `.social-hub-document`.
- No bare `.hub-*` selector may remain in the Observatory style modules.
- No `100vw`, fixed content widths, accidental horizontal overflow, or uncontrolled preformatted blocks.
- Keep the existing dark professional palette but increase depth through restrained surfaces, not decorative noise.
- Use mobile-first layout and progressive desktop enhancement.
- Preserve 44–48px touch targets.
- Add hover only for hover-capable pointers; add `:active` for actual press feedback everywhere relevant.
- Keep `:focus-visible` high contrast and separate from hover.
- Respect reduced motion and forced colors.
- Avoid high z-index escalation; presence remains a bounded separate component.

## UX obligations

- Make Request Context retractable with native `<details>` semantics.
- Summary must explain that context changes inspection, not data.
- Keep all five fields reachable and labeled when expanded.
- Make the human destination read “Open Social Hub”, not the more ambiguous “Interaction Studio”.
- Show semantic capability reality in the hero: 27 safe reads and 5 guarded actions.
- Keep Explore current panel as the primary action and Explore all reads as secondary.
- Keep raw API evidence under Advanced disclosure.
- Keep mutations in a separate Act region with explicit consequence language.

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the Gevurah ownership map, then the Tiferes final file plan before changing markup or CSS.
